Here's what we all need to realize about Star Wars.

It will never be the same, and not only because of the nostalgia factor for us old-timers. If you watch Empire (my fave) and watch any of the new ones - the prequels, or Awakens - there are two things that make them look completely different.

The first is the cinematography. In the new movies, the ships perform like spaceships probably should. In Awakens, in particular, I can tell you that the flight mechanics are pretty top notch. The reason for this difference is because of how the effect was created by ILM 50 years ago. The models were stationary; the camera moved. Today, everything and everyone is doing all the things simultaneously.

Number B: Fidelity of the recording media. The color fidelity of the old film was terrible. Everything was washed. Look at Endor from Jedi. Everything has a pallor to it... and it worked. It helped. Star Wars is a space opera. That's how Lucas described in the initial interviews in the 70s. Operas are grandiose, and timeless, and unrealistic. Consider an analogy:

Opera is to Life as Porn is to Sex and Romantic Comedy is to Relationships.

That color washed, low detail presentation worked for the story that was being told. I think what a lot of people forget about modern incarnations of the classics is that they are not only being made for a new audience, they're being made with new technology. With a medium such as recorded video, the technology used to create it leaves a very real and obvious imprint on the entire thing. A movie isn't just a moving picture book, it's the actors, pictures, sounds and all the shit that was used to capture it.

Would Casablanca have been nearly as good if it was shot in the same style with the same technology as You've Got Mail? No. Not even close.

To add to this the massive contrast between star wars and everything else being made during it's release it astounding. It was so different and told a good story set in a place that no one had ever been to before. It came at the right time and there may never be a movie that captures the entire world like that ever again
